size_pct_nav: $700 million preferred; 9% dividend; $38 conversion after three years; initial weight unknown

drivers.driver: The 9% preferred and scheduled redemption supplied the bulk of the investment's value.
Conversion offered additional participation without requiring a confident common-equity forecast.
Confidence in Gutfreund's ability and integrity was explicit.
drivers.quote: What we do have a strong feeling about is the ability and integrity of John Gutfreund, CEO of Salomon Inc.

drivers.driver: Buffett acknowledged no special insight into investment banking's future profitability.
drivers.quote: We, of course, have no special insights regarding the direction or future profitability of investment banking.

entry_valuation_stated: 9% contractual yield with conversion; ratable redemptions beginning October 31, 1995.
outcome_note: Later crisis required major Buffett intervention; subsequent merger improved the financial outcome. Trust judgment was not vindicated simply by eventual recovery.
sources: Proposed September financing terms reconstructed from transaction account; period report https://www.nytimes.com/1987/09/28/business/salomon-to-sell-12-to-buffett.html used only for preceding-day terms, not later market reaction; fund reference https://www.berkshirehathaway.com/letters/1986.html
pack_quality_notes: Sunday cutoff: prior-day deal terms reconstructed from Monday press. Exact settlement, covenants, prior close and dealer liquidity model unavailable. Perelman threat is context, not one of Buffett's stated economic drivers.
